plan.contextChunk: This figure contains six panels (a through f) arranged in a 3×2 grid, each showing the scalar output y of a trained shallow one-hidden-layer neural network as a function of a scalar input x ∈ [0, 1]. The panels correspond to networks with increasing numbers of hidden units — 6, 7, 8, 10, and 50, plus one additional configuration — with each panel’s title indicating the hidden unit count. Each panel has a horizontal axis labeled “Input, x” and a vertical axis labeled “Output, y”; the y-axis range spans approximately [0, 1] or [−1, 1] depending on the panel. With more hidden units the output function is relatively simple and smooth, while as the hidden unit count decreases the function develops more oscillations and finer local structure. This figure illustrates how the capacity of a shallow neural network — and hence the complexity and expressiveness of the functions it can represent — scales with the number of hidden units.

interactionPlan.concept: The complexity and smoothness of functions a shallow one-hidden-layer network can represent scales with its number of hidden units — too few units overfit with jagged artifacts, while enough units yield a smooth fit to the data.
elements: six panels (a–f) in a 3×2 grid, titled with hidden unit counts (6, 7, 8, 10, 50 hidden units)
panel (a): data only — smooth black ground-truth curve (single smooth hump then trough) with 10 orange scatter points
panel (b): 6 hidden units — teal fitted curve with severe overshoot spikes and kinks, deviating sharply from the black curve
panel (c): 7 hidden units — teal curve still overshooting the peak and undershooting the trough
panel (d): 8 hidden units — teal piecewise-linear-looking curve tracking the data more closely but with visible kinks
panel (e): 10 hidden units — teal curve close to the black curve with mild deviations
panel (f): 50 hidden units — teal curve smooth and closely following the black ground-truth curve
shared axes: x-axis 'Input, x' from 0.0 to 1.0, y-axis 'Output, y' from -1.0 to 1.0
identical 10 orange data points in every panel
identical black ground-truth curve in every panel

interactions.label: Number of hidden units
interactions.teaches: Sweeps network capacity across 6 → 7 → 8 → 10 → 50 hidden units; the learner sees the fitted teal curve morph from unstable, over-shooting jaggedness into a smooth approximation as capacity grows, revealing that hidden unit count controls representable function complexity

interactions.label: Capacity contrast
interactions.teaches: Direct side-by-side contrast between a too-small network whose fit develops wild oscillations and overshoots between data points versus a large network whose fit is smooth and well-behaved

Clicking a panel enlarges it to inspect how closely the fitted curve passes through each orange data point compared to the black ground truth, focusing attention on where a given capacity fails or succeeds

demo_steps.title: The data and the task
demo_steps.narration: Panel (a) shows the target: a smooth black curve sampled at 10 noisy orange points. Every other panel shows a one-hidden-layer network trained to fit these same points.

demo_steps.title: Too little capacity
demo_steps.narration: With only 6 hidden units the fitted teal curve still passes near the points but develops huge overshoots and kinks between them — the network lacks the capacity to represent a smooth solution and settles on an unstable one.

demo_steps.title: Growing capacity
demo_steps.narration: Drag the slider through 7, 8, and 10 units: the spikes shrink, the kinks soften, and the fitted curve progressively hugs the black ground truth.

demo_steps.title: Ample capacity
demo_steps.narration: At 50 hidden units the teal curve is smooth and closely tracks the ground truth — plenty of capacity lets training find a simple, smooth function consistent with the data.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A shallow network's representable function complexity scales with hidden unit count: too few units produce unstable, oscillating fits, while ample units allow smooth functions that generalize well between the training points.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: 3×2 grid of small square panels labeled a) through f); panels b–f carry titles '6 hidden units', '7 hidden units', '8 hidden units', '10 hidden units', '50 hidden units'. Every panel shares the same black smooth ground-truth curve (rise to a peak near x≈0.25 around y≈0.5, then a descent to a shallow trough near x≈0.8 around y≈−0.45) and the same 10 orange/salmon circular scatter points clustered along it. The fitted network curve is light teal: in panel b it spikes far above the plot top around x≈0.3 and plunges below the bottom around x≈0.55 and 0.7; in panel c it overshoots the peak to ~0.8 and undershoots below −1 near x≈0.7; in panel d it is piecewise-linear with kinks and a trough too deep (~−0.8); panels e and f are progressively smoother and closer to black, with f nearly overlapping it. Black axes with ticks at 0.0, 0.5, 1.0 on x and −1.0, 0.0, 1.0 on y; axis labels 'Input, x' and 'Output, y' in italic serif style on the left column panels.

discrepancies: the default (step-0) state fades panels b–e to ~45% opacity and spotlights only the 50-unit panel with a teal border, whereas the source shows all six panels at equal visual weight — the static default no longer reads as a drop-in replacement for the source
panel letters b), c), e), f) are clipped at the canvas edge (drawn at chartArea.left − 14 where there is no y-axis title to leave room), so only the ')' glyph is visible; only a) and d) render fully

the source shows tick marks on every panel (numbers only on the outer edges), but the generated figure removes ticks entirely from the four inner panels and uses inconsistent number formatting ('0', '0.5', '1.0' and y ticks '1/0/−1' instead of the source's uniform '0.0/0.5/1.0', '1.0/0.0/−1.0')
two of the left-cluster data points are placed at x≈0.22 and x≈0.24, nearly overlapping into a single doubled dot, while the source spaces them evenly (~0.17 and ~0.22)
evaluation.notes: All six panels, both curve types, the scatter points, and the capacity-progression narrative are faithfully reproduced with a functional slider/step-player/click-inspect interaction set, but the dimmed-spotlight default composition and the clipped panel letters (b, c, e, f) keep it from reading as a drop-in replacement for the source.
action_items: Fix the panelTag plugin so letters are drawn at a clamped x position (e.g., max(2, chartArea.left − 14) or a fixed offset from the canvas edge) so b), c), e), f) are not clipped.
Change the step-0/default state to show all six panels at full opacity with no highlight border; apply the dim-and-spotlight emphasis only after the user moves the slider or advances the demo.
Restore tick marks on all panels (ticks without numbers on inner panels) and format tick labels consistently with one decimal (0.0/0.5/1.0, 1.0/0.0/−1.0) to match the source.
Re-space the two near-coincident left-cluster data points (0.22/0.24 → roughly 0.17/0.22) to match the source's even spacing.

feedback.rationale: Concept accuracy is 5 and the interaction set works, but concrete implementation defects — clipped panel letters, wrong default opacity, missing/inconsistent ticks, and mis-spaced data points — are all generator-level fixes with no plan changes needed.
